name: 1/√2 scalar
summary: A Z- and an X-spider connected by three wires are the scalar 1/√2.
description:
A phase-free Z-spider and a phase-free X-spider connected by three parallel wires represent the scalar $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$. By the [Hopf rule](../hopf/), two of the three wires can be removed at the cost of a factor ½, leaving the scalar √2 of a single connecting wire.

This is the standard way to write *negative* powers of √2 as a ZX-diagram, as for example needed to normalise the CNOT gate. It is the inverse of the [two-spider scalar](../scalar-state-effect/) for a = 0: placing the two side by side gives the empty diagram.
